questions.question: Write briefly about the spleen as a secondary lymphoid organ.
questions.solution_html:
• The spleen is a major secondary lymphoid organ located in the upper left abdomen. It filters
  • blood and removes old or damaged red blood cells. It also plays an important role in immune
  • response by producing lymphocytes. The spleen traps blood-borne pathogens and helps in
  • antibody production.

questions.question: What is rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.solution_html:
• Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune disease that primarily affects joints. The
  • immune system mistakenly attacks the synovial membrane, causing inflammation. This leads
  • to pain, swelling, and stiffness in joints. Over time, it can result in joint deformity and
  • reduced mobility.

questions.question: Mention two stress-reducing practices that improve immunity.
questions.solution_html:
• Mention two stress-reducing practices that improve immunity.
  • Practices such as regular physical exercise and meditation help reduce stress. Exercise
  • improves circulation and boosts immune cell function. Meditation and yoga reduce cortisol
  • levels, which can suppress immunity. Both practices enhance overall physical and mental
  • health.

questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Describe two differences between jet lag and travel fatigue.
questions.solution_html:
• Jet lag is caused by disruption of the circadian rhythm due to crossing time zones. Travel
  • fatigue results from physical exhaustion during travel. Jet lag affects sleep patterns and
  • hormone cycles, while travel fatigue mainly causes tiredness. Jet lag takes longer to recover
  • compared to travel fatigue.

questions.question: What is infradian rhythm?
questions.solution_html:
• Infradian rhythm refers to biological rhythms with cycles longer than 24 hours. These
  • rhythms occur less frequently than once a day. An example is the menstrual cycle in females.
  • They are regulated by internal biological clocks.
questions.final_answer: They are regulated by internal biological clocks

questions.question: What is meant by biological rhythm in living organisms?
questions.solution_html:
• Biological rhythms are regular cycles of physiological processes in living organisms. They
  • are controlled by internal clocks and environmental cues. These rhythms include circadian
  • infradian, and ultradian rhythms. They help organisms adapt to daily and seasonal changes.
questions.final_answer: infradian, and ultradian rhythms. They help organisms adapt to daily and seasonal changes
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write a short note on environmental zeitgebers.
questions.solution_html:
• Environmental zeitgebers are external cues that help regulate and synchronize the internal
  • biological clock with the external environment. The most important zeitgeber is light, which
  • influences the circadian rhythm by acting on the suprachiasmatic nucleus of the brain. Other
  • zeitgebers include temperature, feeding schedules, physical activity, and social interactions.
  • These cues ensure that physiological processes such as sleep, hormone secretion, and
  • metabolism occur at appropriate times. Disruption of these zeitgebers, such as during shift
  • work or long-distance travel, can lead to circadian rhythm disorders like insomnia and jet lag.
questions.final_answer: work or long-distance travel, can lead to circadian rhythm disorders like insomnia and jet lag
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the role of melatonin in sleep–wake regulation.
questions.solution_html:
• Melatonin is a hormone produced by the pineal gland that plays a crucial role in regulating
  • the sleep–wake cycle. Its secretion is controlled by the suprachiasmatic nucleus and is
  • stimulated by darkness while inhibited by light. Melatonin promotes sleep by lowering body
  • temperature and reducing alertness, thereby preparing the body for rest. It also helps in
  • maintaining the timing and quality of sleep. Any disruption in melatonin secretion, such as
  • exposure to artificial light at night, can disturb sleep patterns and lead to sleep-related
  • disorders.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: What is Type II hypersensitivity and explain antibody-mediated cytotoxicity in / Type II hypersensitivity.
questions.solution_html:
• II hypersensitivity.
  • Type II hypersensitivity is an immune reaction in which antibodies are directed against
  • antigens present on the surface of cells or tissues, leading to their destruction. It is also known
  • as cytotoxic hypersensitivity and involves IgG and IgM antibodies. In antibody-mediated
  • cytotoxicity, these antibodies bind to target cells and activate the complement system
  • resulting in cell lysis. Additionally, immune cells such as natural killer cells may destroy the
  • antibody-coated cells through antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). This
  • mechanism is seen in conditions like hemolytic anemia and mismatched blood transfusion
  • reactions.

questions.question: Define secondary sexual characteristics. Enumerate the secondary sexual / characteristics in females.
questions.solution_html:
• characteristics in females.
  • Secondary sexual characteristics are physical features that develop during puberty under the
  • influence of sex hormones and distinguish the two sexes, though they are not directly
  • involved in reproduction. In females, estrogen plays a major role in the development of these
  • characteristics. These include enlargement of breasts, widening of hips, and increased
  • deposition of subcutaneous fat, especially in the thighs and buttocks. Growth of pubic and
  • axillary hair and the onset of menstruation are also important features. These changes indicate
  • sexual maturity and prepare the body for reproductive functions.
questions.final_answer: sexual maturity and prepare the body for reproductive functions
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Describe female fetal sex differentiation with reference to genetic makeup and / hormonal environment.
questions.solution_html:
• hormonal environment.
  • Female fetal sex differentiation is primarily determined by genetic and hormonal factors. In
  • the absence of a Y chromosome and the SRY gene, the undifferentiated gonads develop into
  • ovaries. Since there is no secretion of testosterone or anti-Müllerian hormone, the Müllerian
  • ducts persist and develop into female reproductive structures such as the uterus, fallopian
  • tubes, and upper vagina. The Wolffian ducts regress due to the lack of male hormones. Thus
  • the default developmental pathway leads to female differentiation when male-specific
  • hormonal influences are absent.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Enumerate the principal features of adaptive immunity and explain their / significance.
questions.solution_html:
• Enumerate the principal features of adaptive immunity and explain their
  • significance.
  • Adaptive immunity is a highly specialized defense mechanism characterized by specificity
  • memory, diversity, and self/non-self recognition. It involves lymphocytes, particularly B cells
  • and T cells, which respond specifically to particular antigens. One of its key features is
  • immunological memory, which allows the body to respond more rapidly and effectively upon
  • subsequent exposure to the same antigen. It also has the ability to distinguish between the
  • body’s own cells and foreign invaders, preventing autoimmune reactions. These features
  • make adaptive immunity highly efficient in providing long-term protection and are the basis
  • for vaccination.

  • immunological memory, which allows the body to respond more rapidly and effectively upon
  • subsequent exposure to the same antigen. It also has the ability to distinguish between the
  • body’s own cells and foreign invaders, preventing autoimmune reactions. These features
  • make adaptive immunity highly efficient in providing long-term protection and are the basis
